title: Commands of God
definition: The Commands of God are His authoritative instructions that reveal His will and call His people to faithful obedience.
summary: The Commands of God are His authoritative instructions that reveal His will and call His people to faithful obedience.
christFocus: Jesus perfectly obeyed the Father, fulfilled what sinners failed to keep, and teaches His disciples to obey His commands through love and dependence on Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s commands are not random burdens. They reveal His holy character, His good design, and the path of faithful living. Because God is good, His commands are good, even when obedience is costly.

Scripture shows that obedience cannot save sinners; only Christ can. Yet saved people are called to obey. The Gospel does not remove God’s commands as if holiness no longer matters. It gives believers a new heart, the Holy Spirit, and a new desire to walk in God’s ways.

Jesus shows the true shape of obedience. He obeyed from love, trusted the Father fully, and gave Himself for sinners. In Christ, God’s commands become the path of discipleship, not a ladder for earning acceptance.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people hear commands and think only of shame, control, or religious pressure. Others reject commands because they confuse grace with self-rule. Scripture corrects both errors by showing obedience as the fruit of belonging to Christ.

This doctrine helps church-hurt believers distinguish God’s good commands from human control. It also helps recovering believers see that Christ calls them into a new way of life, not merely into forgiven habits.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not obey to earn God’s love; obey because you have been loved in Christ. Ask the Holy Spirit to make God’s commands clear, convict you where you resist, and strengthen you to take practical steps of repentance, faithfulness, and love.
